cards.front: Recall a key point about Quality
cards.back: Quality control (QC) inspects the finished product to detect defects - it's reactive and occurs after production. Defective items are rejected or reworked.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Quality
cards.back: Quality assurance (QA) builds quality into every stage of the production process - it's proactive and aims to prevent defects before they occur.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Quality
cards.back: Total quality management (TQM) involves every employee in continuous quality improvement: zero defects culture, employee empowerment, and customer focus throughout the organisation.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Quality
cards.back: ISO 9001 is an international quality standard: businesses must document processes, demonstrate consistent quality, and pass regular audits. Certification builds customer trust.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Quality
cards.back: Higher quality reduces costs long-term: fewer returns, less rework, better reputation, more repeat business, and ability to charge premium prices.

cards.front: What should you know about business exam tips?
cards.back: When evaluating quality systems, use the PAC framework: Prevention (how does it stop defects?), Assurance (how does it build customer confidence?), Cost (do the benefits outweigh the investment?). Quality always has a cost, but poor quality costs more.

Students often make mistakes here. Wrong: High-quality products always cost more to produce than low-quality products. Correct: While high-quality materials may cost more, quality systems often REDUCE total costs by eliminating: rework (fixing defects), returns and refunds, warranty claims, lost customers, and wasted materials. AO1 — Knowledge: Demonstrate knowledge of Quality with precise business/economic terminology. Define key terms and state accurate factual information.

Quality is a key topic in GCSE Business Studies that affects how businesses operate in the UK economy. Understanding this concept requires knowledge of both theoretical principles and real-world application. The AQA specification requires you to explain, analyse and evaluate business concepts using appropriate terminology, and apply them to real business scenarios using UK examples.

cards.front: Applying Quality to UK Business Examples
cards.back: For quality, applying theory to practice means using real UK business examples to illustrate your understanding. Small businesses face different challenges from large corporations when dealing with quality. Consider how factors like business size, ownership structure, industry sector and market position affect the impact of quality on a business.

GCSE Business exam questions about quality range from 1-mark definition questions to 12-mark evaluation questions. For definition questions (1-2 marks), give a precise business definition. For explanation questions (3-4 marks), define and explain with a brief example. For analysis questions (6-9 marks), develop a chain of reasoning showing cause and effect.
